acip: GNYIS PA ZHAR BYUNG RGYA JA'I MCHOD PA NI, GUR GUM MDANGS LDAN SOGS RKANG PA GNYIS TE (GUR GUM) GYI (MDANGS) MDOG LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR SER DANG (LDAN) ZHING (BZANG PO) SHIN TU DRI ZHIM PO'I DRI NGAD CAN (RO BRGYA) STE RO BCUD MANG PO DANG LDAN PA'I (DPAL 'DZIN) PA STE YOD PA'I (RGYA JA'I BTUNG BA) RNAMS KYANG 'BUL LO,,
wylie: gnyis pa zhar byung rgya ja'i mchod pa ni, gur gum mdangs ldan sogs rkang pa gnyis te (gur gum) gyi (mdangs) mdog lta bu kha dog dmar ser dang (ldan) zhing (bzang po) shin tu dri zhim po'i dri ngad can (ro brgya) ste ro bcud mang po dang ldan pa'i (dpal 'dzin) pa ste yod pa'i (rgya ja'i btung ba) rnams kyang 'bul lo
english: This brings us to our second point from above: an incidental offering of fine Chinese tea.  This is presented in the three lines that mention tea "of a saffron hue."  And so here I offer cups of the tea from China which is of the finest sort--which possesses or gives off the finest, most delightful fragrance: a truly delicious scent.  This tea is laden with a thousand flavors, meaning that it has many different tastes at its heart, and has a reddish golden color similar to the hue of saffron.
